items.text: Page titles are different. A leads with the product category, and B adds the parent brand at the end.
items.evidence: A title: 'Home Designer | Home Design Software for DIY'; B title: 'Home Designer Software for DIY | Chief Architect'

items.text: A uses the Open Sans webfont plus an icon font. B uses the system-ui font stack.
items.evidence: A fonts_by_element_count: Open Sans 591, caicon 18; B: system-ui 316, Arial 1

items.text: B's body text is slightly larger and has more line spacing.
items.evidence: A body 16px/24px; B body 17px/28.05px

items.text: The color palettes differ. A uses a light cyan blue, a lime green and gray panels. B uses navy, dark blue and an orange accent.
Body text color is neutral near-black in A and a blue-tinted dark slate in B.

items.text: A's primary button is transparent with a white outline and square corners. B's primary button is solid orange with rounded corners.

items.text: A's headings are all light weight (300) at large sizes (h2 37px). B's headings are bold (h2 weight 700 at 33.6px). The overall typographic voice differs from light and airy to heavy and compact.
B has no broken images. All 6 images have valid natural sizes. There is no hero photograph or comparison matrix.
items.evidence: B images all have natural [130,184] or [348,492] and file names. B has no zero-size entries.

items.text: B's content container has a consistent left edge at x≈180 with a max width of about 1080px. A's content is inset at about x=235, and the hero image runs from 220 to 1220.
items.evidence: B slices: headings at x=180, footer rule 180-1260. A slices: text at x=235, image rect x220 w1000.

items.text: A's heading outline skips levels. h1 is followed directly by h3 ('Download', 'Explore', 'Learn'), and an h4 is followed by h2. B also has h1 then h3, but its footer column titles are h4 and its product names are h3.

items.text: A's DOM is much heavier: 118 divs, 25 scripts, 9 style blocks, 6 stylesheets, 8 inline SVGs, 6 noscript and a <base> tag. B has 45 divs, 1 script, 1 style block, 0 stylesheets and 0 SVGs.
items.evidence: tag_counts A: div 118, script 25, style 9, svg 8, noscript 6, base 1. B: div 45, script 1, style 1, svg 0.

items.text: A's CSS uses many classes (432 total, 148 unique). B uses far fewer (72 total, 31 unique). Both have a low Tailwind-like fraction (A 0.081, B 0.014).
items.evidence: classes in facts.

items.text: A's icons are font glyphs from 'caicon'. In the screenshots they render as empty box placeholders in the search bar, the Rent/Buy tiles, the Compare Features button and the social icons. B has no icon glyphs. Its social links are plain text names (HomeTalk, Blog, Facebook, YouTube, Instagram, Houzz, Pinterest).
items.evidence: A slice 0, 1 and 3 show square placeholder glyphs. B slice 3 footer row of text links. caicon on 18 elements.

items.text: Footer columns differ slightly in copy. B's Company list reads 'Contact Us', where A's reads 'Contact Us - Social'. B adds social/community text links (HomeTalk, Blog, Facebook, YouTube, Instagram, Houzz, Pinterest) in the footer.
items.evidence: A slice 3 'Contact Us - Social'. B slice 3 last Company item and the link row.

features.statement: Typography uses the system-ui font stack rather than a custom webfont.
Body text is slightly larger with generous line spacing, around 17px on 28px line height.
Headings are bold (700) and compact rather than light and airy.
Palette is navy and dark blue with a single orange accent and pale blue-gray panels.
Body text color is a blue-tinted dark slate rather than neutral black.
Primary call-to-action buttons are solid orange fills with rounded corners.
Rounded corners are used widely across cards, buttons and images.
Hero section has a dark-blue gradient background that lightens toward one side.
Product images are large, with drop shadows and rounded edges.
Header has a dark utility strip, small bold text logo and right-aligned nav with caret markers, no search field.
Hero includes two side-by-side CTA buttons: a solid primary and an outlined secondary.
Footer column headings are small uppercase letter-spaced labels with left-aligned links.
Intro copy and link lists are arranged in multi-column CSS grid layouts.
Products appear as bordered white cards in a row, with a separate horizontal promo bar below.
Secondary actions are outlined buttons stacked above or beside the primary button, instead of plain text links.
Strikethrough old prices use the semantic <s> element.
Product names and section titles are real heading elements, with footer column titles as h4.
Section headings use sentence/title case rather than all caps.
Purchase options use a centered segmented toggle with active selects and a clear 'Choose a product' heading.
Footer is dark navy with bold white column headings and social networks listed as plain text links.
Page uses semantic <main> and <figure> elements and real <button> elements.
Inline body links are underlined.
All images load correctly with valid sizes; no broken images or icon-font glyphs.
Content sits in a consistent left-aligned container about 1080px wide.
Markup is lean, with few divs, one script, one style block, no SVGs and few classes.
Page title appends the parent brand name at the end after a pipe separator.
Supporting sub-headings are merged into the main content block rather than standing as separate large-heading sections.
